applicability_scope: User-reported Level 1 review of all nine current P17 Overview theorems and every recursively statement-relevant definition.
Theorem 5.1: Existence of an element generator for every indexed infinite-language family, under vanishing noise and arbitrary omissions.
Theorem 5.4: Constant-noise generation is equivalent to the finite-subcollection condition, for an explicitly enumerated infinite-language class and 0 < c < 1.
Theorem 6.1: The named finite-expansion Algorithm-5 generator eventually produces infinite fresh valid sets and attains set-based upper density at least 1 - c.
Theorem 6.4: The explicit two-language witness rules out any upper-density guarantee strictly above 1 - c, for 0 < c < 1.
Theorem 6.5: Infinite-set generation with lower density under finite contamination is equivalent to the pairwise finite-difference density condition.
Theorem 6.11: The vanishing-noise set-density characterization for explicitly indexed infinite languages and supplied target orders.
Theorem 6.14: The constant-noise set-density characterization on 0 < c < 1 and positive rho; the source c = 1 endpoint is outside the statement.

Theorem 6.18: The conditional finite-expansion transfer for element-density guarantees, using internally constructed canonical natural-number orders and internally proved finite-change density invariance.

Theorem 7.8: The named Algorithm-9 set generator is eventually fresh and valid and each sufficiently late output set has lower density at least (1 - epsilon) / M under vanishing noise and bounded displacement.

Finite histories, indexed infinite families, OracleFamily, validity/freshness, noise/omission/presentation regimes, ordered and set/element density, finite intersections, finite expansion, canonical natural orders, explicit floor-increment witnesses, Algorithm-5/9 defining interfaces and bounded displacement.

Named algorithms are reviewed for statement meaning only. Canonical equal-type presentations count as the same reviewed statements. Definition-11 review on the grouped Proposition-7.4/Lemma-7.5 card does not review those statements.
